title: Public-private partnership to bring new exhaust system to DIII-D
summary: The DIII-D National Fusion Facility announced last week that it will partner with Kyoto Fusioneering to design, manufacture, install, and operate a new power exhaust system in the DIII-D tokamak to advance a negative triangularity approach for commercialization. This effort builds on the company’s partnership with Oak Ridge National Laboratory, which was announced earlier this year.

title: Maritime Nuclear Startup Bluecore Buys First Uranium For Nuclear Plants On Barges
summary: Bluecore Energy, the Long Beach, US-based floating nuclear power startup, has bought its first supply of uranium hexafluoride (UF6), a low-enriched 4.95% blend of U-235 suitable for a commercial nuclear power installation. The material is being held at a US nuclear fuel facility outside the state of California while Bluecore advances its plans for future fuel fabrication, testing and validation. UF6 is the required form of uranium during the enrichment stage of the nuclear fuel cycle. During the fuel fabrication stage, the UF6 is converted into uranium dioxide, or UO2, which can then be fabricated into fuel pellets and assembled into nuclear fuel. The purchase follows Bluecore’s recent $50m (€44m) seed financing.

title: ABS, DOE-NE sign maritime nuclear MOU
summary: The American Bureau of Shipping and the Department of Energy’s Office of Nuclear Energy have signed a memorandum of understanding to advance modern commercial nuclear technology at sea, whether as floating nuclear power plants; nuclear-powered vessels; or at ports, shipyards, or industrial bases.

title: Entergy Texas’ Orange County Advanced Power Station begins delivering reliable power to Southeast Texas
summary: Entergy Texas officially placed its Orange County Advanced Power Station into service today, adding a new source of around-the-clock power to help meet the growing energy needs across Southeast Texas. title: Bangladesh’s Rooppur-1 Nuclear Plant Achieves First Criticality
summary: Unit 1 at the Rooppur nuclear power station being built by Russia in Bangladesh has achieved criticality with grid connection expected by the end of November. The 1,080-MW VVER V-523 pressurised water reactor unit, construction of which began in 2017, achieved first criticality at 15:34 on 11 October. First criticality is the milestone moment when a nuclear reactor achieves a self-sustaining, controlled chain reaction for the very first time. Rooppur, Bangladesh’s most expensive infrastructure facility, has considerable backing from Russia. Moscow is financing $11.9bn (€10.6bn) in state loans for the project, which has been estimated to cost up to $12.8bn.
